item.title: Using a Linux Laptop as a Hotspot for a PS5
item.description:
It was Thanksgiving week, and with Black Friday happening, I finally decided to get a PS5. I didn’t expect it to feel like such a big moment, but walking out of Best Buy with the box in hand was surprisingly exciting—almost like driving off with a new car. I even buckled it into the passenger seat on the way home.

Once I got back, though, I ran into a small issue. To connect the PS5 to the university Wi-Fi, I needed to register its MAC address on iprequest.stanford.edu. Unfortunately, the site was down at the time. Since my laptop was already registered and had internet access, I found a workaround: I set up a Wi-Fi hotspot on my laptop and shared the connection with the PS5. It worked smoothly, and I was able to get everything up and running without much delay.
